title: Mechanics II
topics: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 108 rad/s in 4 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 108 / 4 = 27 rad/s squared.

items.q: A force of 200 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.8 m from the axis of a nut. Calculate the turning moment about the axis in N m.
items.s: Turning moment = force x perpendicular distance = 200 x 0.8 = 160 N m.

items.q: A uniform disc of mass 2.5 kg and radius 0.2 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its face. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a disc about its central axis the moment of inertia is half the mass times the radius squared, so 2.5 x 0.2 x 0.2 / 2 = 0.05.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 0.6 kg m squared turns at 15 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 0.6 x 15 = 9 kg m squared per s.

items.q: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 8 m below the surface of a liquid of density 800 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and give your answer in kPa.
items.s: Pressure = density x g x depth = 800 x 9.8 x 8 = 62.72 kPa.

items.q: A pressure of 400 Pa acts on a surface of area 0.5 m squared. Calculate the force acting normally on the surface in N.
items.s: Force = pressure x area = 400 x 0.5 = 200 N.

items.q: Water flows along a pipe of cross sectional area 40 cm squared at 2 m/s. The pipe narrows to a cross sectional area of 2 cm squared. Calculate the speed of the water in the narrow section in m/s.
items.s: The product of area and speed is constant, so the new speed is 40 x 2 / 2 = 40 m/s.

items.q: A liquid flows through a pipe of cross sectional area 4 cm squared at a speed of 3 m/s. Calculate the volume delivered per second in cm cubed per s.
items.s: Volume per second = area x speed = 4 cm squared x 3 m/s, with 3 m equal to 300 cm, giving 12 cm cubed per s.

items.q: A trolley of mass 3 kg moves at 15 m/s. Calculate its linear momentum in kg m/s.
items.s: Linear momentum = mass x velocity = 3 x 15 = 45 kg m/s.

items.q: An engine runs at 480 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed in radians per second, taking pi as 3.142.
items.s: One revolution is 2 x 3.142 rad and one minute is 60 s, so the angular speed is (480 x 6.284)/60 = 50.27 rad/s.

items.q: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 1.5 m moves with a speed of 10 m/s. Calculate the angular speed of the wheel in rad/s.
items.s: Angular speed = speed of the rim / radius = 10 / 1.5 = 6.67 rad/s.

items.q: A body of mass 18 kg moves in a circle of radius 10 m at a steady speed of 2 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it in N.
items.s: Centripetal force = mass x speed squared / radius = 18 x 2 x 2 / 10 = 7.2 N.

items.q: A force of 100 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.6 m at 30 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 100 x 0.6 x sin 30 degrees = 30 N m.

items.q: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. A mass of 50 g hangs 15 cm from the pivot on one side. At what distance in cm from the pivot must a mass of 40 g be hung on the other side to balance the rule?
items.s: Balancing the turning effects, 50 x 15 = 40 x d, so d = 750/40 = 18.75 cm.

items.q: Two equal and opposite forces of 40 N each act at two points 0.6 m apart on a body. Calculate the turning effect of the couple in N m.
items.s: The turning effect of a couple is one force times the full separation of the two lines of action, so 40 x 1.2 = 48 N m.

items.q: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 0.25 m turns about a diameter. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a solid sphere about a diameter the value is two fifths of the mass times the radius squared, giving 0.125.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 1.5 kg and length 0.8 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a rod about its centre the value is mass times length squared divided by 12 = 1.5 x 0.8 x 0.8 / 12 = 0.08.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 1.5 kg and length 1.2 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 1.5 x 1.2 x 1.2 / 3 = 0.72.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of mass 2.5 kg has a moment of inertia of 0.4 kg m squared about an axis through its centre of mass. Calculate its moment of inertia about a parallel axis 0.3 m from that one, in kg m squared.
items.s: The parallel axis rule adds mass times the square of the separation: 0.4 + 2.5 x 0.3 x 0.3 = 0.625.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.5 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 25 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 25 x 0.5 = 12.5 m/s.

items.q: A solid disc of mass 3 kg rolls without slipping along a level surface at 10 m/s. Calculate its total kinetic energy in J.
items.s: A rolling disc carries half its energy as motion of the centre and half as turning, so the total is three quarters of the mass times the speed squared = 225 J.

items.q: A flywheel of moment of inertia 2 kg m squared turns at 6 rad/s. Calculate its rotational kinetic energy in J.
items.s: Rotational kinetic energy = half the moment of inertia times the angular speed squared = 2 x 6 x 6 / 2 = 36 J.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 8 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 200 N at 2 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 200 x 6 / 8 = 150 N.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 5 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 800 N at 2.5 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 800 x 2.5 / 5 = 400 N.

items.q: Two planets of masses 1 x 10^24 kg and 8 x 10^22 kg have their centres 1.5 x 10^8 m apart. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the force between them in units of 10^19 N.
items.s: Force = gravitational constant x product of the masses / distance squared = 6.67 x 1 x 8 / (1.5 x 1.5) = 23.72 units of 10^19 N.

items.q: A planet has a mass of 5 x 10^22 kg and a radius of 6 x 10^6 m. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the escape speed from its surface in km/s.
items.s: Escape speed is the square root of twice the gravitational constant times the mass divided by the radius, giving 1.05 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 8 x 10^7 m about a planet of mass 4 x 10^25 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate its orbital speed in km/s.
items.s: Orbital speed is the square root of the gravitational constant times the planet mass divided by the orbit radius, giving 5.77 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 5 x 10^7 m about a planet of mass 5 x 10^25 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared and pi as 3.142, calculate the period of the orbit in hours.
items.s: The period is twice pi times the square root of the cube of the radius divided by the gravitational constant times the planet mass, which is 10.69 hours.

items.q: A planet moves round the sun at a mean distance of 1.5 x 10^11 m with a period of 8 years. A second planet moves at 8 x 10^11 m. Calculate the period of the second planet in years.
items.s: The square of the period varies as the cube of the radius, so the new period is 8 x (8/1.5) raised to 1.5 = 98.53 years.

items.q: A wire of length 2.5 m and cross sectional area 1 x 10^-6 m squared extends by 0.5 mm when a load of 50 N hangs on it. Calculate the Young modulus of the material in units of 10^10 Pa.
items.s: Stress = 50 / (1 x 10^-6) and strain = 0.5 x 10^-3 / 2.5, so the modulus is stress divided by strain = 25 units of 10^10 Pa.

items.q: A wire of original length 2 m is stretched by 1.5 mm. Calculate the tensile strain produced.
items.s: Strain is the extension divided by the original length = 0.0015 / 2 = 0.00075.

items.q: A load of 400 N hangs on a wire of cross sectional area 1.5 x 10^-6 m squared. Calculate the stress in the wire in units of 10^6 Pa.
items.s: Stress = force / area = 400 / (1.5 x 10^-6) = 266.7 units of 10^6 Pa.

items.q: A body of volume 300 cm cubed is fully immersed in water of density 1000 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the upthrust on the body in N.
items.s: The upthrust equals the weight of water displaced = 1000 x (300 x 10^-6) x 9.8 = 2.94 N.

items.q: A solid of mass 60 g has a volume of 125 cm cubed. Calculate its density relative to water.
items.s: Relative density is the mass in grams divided by the volume in cm cubed, so 60 / 125 = 0.48.

items.q: A tank contains water and has a small hole 2.5 m below the surface. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the speed at which the water leaves the hole in m/s.
items.s: The water leaves with the speed gained in falling that depth, the square root of 2 x 9.8 x 2.5 = 7 m/s.

items.q: A liquid of density 1000 kg/m cubed is forced through a horizontal pipe by a pressure difference of 6000 Pa. Calculate the speed it attains in m/s.
items.s: The pressure difference appears as kinetic energy per unit volume, so the speed is the square root of 2 x 6000 / 1000 = 3.46 m/s.

items.q: A body of mass 0.5 kg moving at 8 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 2.5 kg and the two move off together. Calculate their common speed in m/s.
items.s: Momentum before equals momentum after, so the common speed is 0.5 x 8 / (0.5 + 2.5) = 1.33 m/s.

items.q: A force acts for 0.5 s on a body of mass 1.5 kg and changes its speed from 2 m/s to 12 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the force in N.
items.s: Impulse equals change of momentum, so force = 1.5 x (12 - 2) / 0.5 = 30 N.

items.q: A ball moving at 5 m/s overtakes another moving at 3 m/s in the same direction. If the coefficient of restitution is 0.5, calculate their relative speed of separation in m/s.
items.s: Relative speed of separation = coefficient of restitution x relative speed of approach = 0.5 x (5 - 3) = 1 m/s.

items.q: A flywheel turns at a steady angular speed of 40 rad/s for 9 s. Calculate the angle turned through in radians.
items.s: Angle turned = angular speed x time = 40 x 9 = 360 rad.

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 156 rad/s in 4 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 156 / 4 = 39 rad/s squared.

items.q: A force of 120 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.6 m from the axis of a nut. Calculate the turning moment about the axis in N m.
items.s: Turning moment = force x perpendicular distance = 120 x 0.6 = 72 N m.

items.q: A uniform disc of mass 4 kg and radius 0.6 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its face. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a disc about its central axis the moment of inertia is half the mass times the radius squared, so 4 x 0.6 x 0.6 / 2 = 0.72.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 1.2 kg m squared turns at 4 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 1.2 x 4 = 4.8 kg m squared per s.

items.q: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 3 m below the surface of a liquid of density 1200 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and give your answer in kPa.
items.s: Pressure = density x g x depth = 1200 x 9.8 x 3 = 35.28 kPa.

items.q: A pressure of 200 Pa acts on a surface of area 0.05 m squared. Calculate the force acting normally on the surface in N.
items.s: Force = pressure x area = 200 x 0.05 = 10 N.

items.q: Water flows along a pipe of cross sectional area 10 cm squared at 3 m/s. The pipe narrows to a cross sectional area of 8 cm squared. Calculate the speed of the water in the narrow section in m/s.
items.s: The product of area and speed is constant, so the new speed is 10 x 3 / 8 = 3.75 m/s.

items.q: A liquid flows through a pipe of cross sectional area 10 cm squared at a speed of 1.5 m/s. Calculate the volume delivered per second in cm cubed per s.
items.s: Volume per second = area x speed = 10 cm squared x 1.5 m/s, with 1.5 m equal to 150 cm, giving 15 cm cubed per s.

items.q: A trolley of mass 1 kg moves at 8 m/s. Calculate its linear momentum in kg m/s.
items.s: Linear momentum = mass x velocity = 1 x 8 = 8 kg m/s.

items.q: An engine runs at 90 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed in radians per second, taking pi as 3.142.
items.s: One revolution is 2 x 3.142 rad and one minute is 60 s, so the angular speed is (90 x 6.284)/60 = 9.43 rad/s.

items.q: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 0.25 m moves with a speed of 8 m/s. Calculate the angular speed of the wheel in rad/s.
items.s: Angular speed = speed of the rim / radius = 8 / 0.25 = 32 rad/s.

items.q: A body of mass 11 kg moves in a circle of radius 7 m at a steady speed of 7 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it in N.
items.s: Centripetal force = mass x speed squared / radius = 11 x 7 x 7 / 7 = 77 N.

items.q: A force of 20 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.4 m at 45 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 20 x 0.4 x sin 45 degrees = 5.66 N m.

items.q: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. A mass of 20 g hangs 15 cm from the pivot on one side. At what distance in cm from the pivot must a mass of 40 g be hung on the other side to balance the rule?
items.s: Balancing the turning effects, 20 x 15 = 40 x d, so d = 300/40 = 7.5 cm.

items.q: A solid sphere of mass 4 kg and radius 0.5 m turns about a diameter. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a solid sphere about a diameter the value is two fifths of the mass times the radius squared, giving 0.4.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 0.6 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a rod about its centre the value is mass times length squared divided by 12 = 3 x 0.6 x 0.6 / 12 = 0.09.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 4 kg and length 0.6 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 4 x 0.6 x 0.6 / 3 = 0.48.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of mass 2.5 kg has a moment of inertia of 0.2 kg m squared about an axis through its centre of mass. Calculate its moment of inertia about a parallel axis 0.4 m from that one, in kg m squared.
items.s: The parallel axis rule adds mass times the square of the separation: 0.2 + 2.5 x 0.4 x 0.4 = 0.6.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.4 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 5 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 5 x 0.4 = 2 m/s.

items.q: A solid disc of mass 4 kg rolls without slipping along a level surface at 2 m/s. Calculate its total kinetic energy in J.
items.s: A rolling disc carries half its energy as motion of the centre and half as turning, so the total is three quarters of the mass times the speed squared = 12 J.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines principle of moments?
o: the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
a flat sheet whose depth is negligible compared with its length and breadth
the turning effect of a force about an axis, equal to the force times its perpendicular distance from that axis
the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart
items.s: principle of moments: the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect. The other options describe breaking strength, torque, thin lamina.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines unstable equilibrium?
o: the rule that the volume delivered through a narrow tube varies as the fourth power of the radius
movement of a round body along a surface while it also turns about its own axis
the upward push of a fluid on a body partly or wholly immersed in it
a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement
items.s: unstable equilibrium: a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement. The other options describe Poiseuille law, rolling motion, upthrust.

items.q: coefficient of restitution may be defined as
o: a head-on meeting of bodies after which they move together with some kinetic energy lost as heat
the product of the mass of a body and its velocity
the ratio of the relative rate of separation after a bounce to the relative rate of approach before it
the internal rubbing in a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another
items.s: coefficient of restitution: the ratio of the relative rate of separation after a bounce to the relative rate of approach before it. The other options describe inelastic collision, viscosity, linear momentum.

items.q: Which of the following best describes conservation of angular momentum?
o: a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement
the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts
the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
the ratio of the force per unit area to the fractional extension of a wire, a measure of stiffness
items.s: conservation of angular momentum: the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts. The other options describe Young modulus, unstable equilibrium, radian.

items.q: Which term is described by “movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel”?
o: period of revolution
angular displacement
angular acceleration
uniform circular motion
items.s: uniform circular motion is movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel.

items.q: Which of the following best describes moment arm?
o: the steady rate of fall reached when the upward drag balances the weight of a falling body
the way the material of a body is spread out relative to the axis about which it turns
the perpendicular distance from the axis of turning to the line along which a force acts
the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
items.s: moment arm: the perpendicular distance from the axis of turning to the line along which a force acts. The other options describe terminal speed, mass distribution, radian.

items.q: Which of the following best describes relative density?
o: the rule that the upward push equals the weight of fluid displaced by an immersed body
the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water
the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
the internal rubbing in a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another
items.s: relative density: the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water. The other options describe buoyancy law, viscosity, principle of moments.

items.q: radian may be defined as
o: the pull of a planet on a body, equal to the product of its mass and the local field strength
the rule that the product of cross section and speed stays the same along a pipe carrying an incompressible fluid
the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
the ability of a material to be drawn out into a long thin thread
items.s: radian: the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius. The other options describe ductility, weight, equation of continuity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes angular impulse?
o: the product of an applied turning effect and the time for which it acts on a rotating body
one complete journey of a body round an external centre
the internal rubbing in a fluid that resists the sliding of one layer over another
a rapidly spinning heavy wheel whose axis keeps its direction when the frame is tilted
items.s: angular impulse: the product of an applied turning effect and the time for which it acts on a rotating body. The other options describe gyroscope, revolution, viscosity.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rule that the product of cross section and speed stays the same along a pipe carrying an incompressible fluid”?
o: viscosity
equation of continuity
Bernoulli theorem
terminal speed
items.s: equation of continuity is the rule that the product of cross section and speed stays the same along a pipe carrying an incompressible fluid.

items.q: All of the following belong to Torque and rotational dynamics EXCEPT
o: torque
ideal fluid
couple
moment arm
items.s: Every other option belongs to Torque and rotational dynamics. “ideal fluid” belongs to Fluid dynamics, not Torque and rotational dynamics.

items.q: The statement “the rule that the square of the time of one circuit varies as the cube of the radius” describes which of the following?
o: geostationary orbit
period distance relation
escape speed
orbital speed
items.s: period distance relation is the rule that the square of the time of one circuit varies as the cube of the radius.

items.q: The statement “the fractional change in length, volume or shape produced by an applied force” describes which of the following?
o: strain
elastic limit
breaking strength
Young modulus
items.s: strain is the fractional change in length, volume or shape produced by an applied force.

items.q: Which of the following best describes conservation of linear momentum?
o: a resting state in which a small displacement creates a restoring turning effect back to the original position
the rate at which a turning effect does work on a rotating body
the principle that the total quantity of motion of an isolated system does not change during an interaction
the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water
items.s: conservation of linear momentum: the principle that the total quantity of motion of an isolated system does not change during an interaction. The other options describe rotational power, stable equilibrium, relative density.

items.q: Which term is described by “the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone”?
o: conservation of angular momentum
rolling motion
precession
gyroscope
items.s: precession is the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone.

items.q: The statement “the product of the turning resistance of a body about an axis and its rate of turning about that axis” describes which of the following?
o: angular momentum
condition for pure rolling
spin
conservation of angular momentum
items.s: angular momentum is the product of the turning resistance of a body about an axis and its rate of turning about that axis.

items.q: Which of the following best describes rotational equilibrium?
o: the state in which the total turning effect on a body about any axis is zero
the fractional change in length, volume or shape produced by an applied force
a rapidly spinning heavy wheel whose axis keeps its direction when the frame is tilted
the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point
items.s: rotational equilibrium: the state in which the total turning effect on a body about any axis is zero. The other options describe gravitational potential, strain, gyroscope.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines rotational equilibrium?
o: the ability of a material to be drawn out into a long thin thread
the state in which the total turning effect on a body about any axis is zero
the point about which a floating body begins to turn when tilted slightly
a head-on meeting of bodies in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
items.s: rotational equilibrium: the state in which the total turning effect on a body about any axis is zero. The other options describe metacentre, ductility, elastic collision.

items.q: thin lamina may be defined as
o: the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone
a machine in which pressure applied to a small piston is transmitted to give a large force on a bigger piston
the turning of a body about an axis that passes through its own centre
a flat sheet whose depth is negligible compared with its length and breadth
items.s: thin lamina: a flat sheet whose depth is negligible compared with its length and breadth. The other options describe hydraulic press, precession, spin.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: Which statement correctly defines yield point?
o: the point about which a floating body begins to turn when tilted slightly
the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull
the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart
items.s: yield point: the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull. The other options describe principle of moments, metacentre, breaking strength.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines uniform circular motion?
o: movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel
a flat sheet whose depth is negligible compared with its length and breadth
the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts
the force acting per unit cross sectional area of a stretched or compressed material
items.s: uniform circular motion: movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel. The other options describe conservation of angular momentum, stress, thin lamina.

items.q: universal gravitational attraction may be defined as
o: the way the material of a body is spread out relative to the axis about which it turns
the rule that the pull between two masses falls as the square of the distance between their centres
the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
the pull of a planet on a body, equal to the product of its mass and the local field strength
items.s: universal gravitational attraction: the rule that the pull between two masses falls as the square of the distance between their centres. The other options describe mass distribution, angular velocity, weight.

items.q: gravitational field strength may be defined as
o: the pull per unit mass experienced by a small body placed at a point
the ratio of the relative rate of separation after a bounce to the relative rate of approach before it
the point about which a floating body begins to turn when tilted slightly
the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
items.s: gravitational field strength: the pull per unit mass experienced by a small body placed at a point. The other options describe principle of moments, metacentre, coefficient of restitution.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines geostationary orbit?
o: the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart
a resting state in which a small displacement creates a restoring turning effect back to the original position
a closed path above the equator in which a satellite takes one day and stays over one point
the point about which a floating body begins to turn when tilted slightly
items.s: geostationary orbit: a closed path above the equator in which a satellite takes one day and stays over one point. The other options describe breaking strength, stable equilibrium, metacentre.

items.q: The statement “the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point” describes which of the following?
o: orbital speed
universal gravitational attraction
gravitational potential
geostationary orbit
items.s: gravitational potential is the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines terminal speed.
o: the steady rate of fall reached when the upward drag balances the weight of a falling body
the rule that the pressure plus the kinetic and potential energy per unit volume stays constant along a tube of flow
a heavy wheel fixed to a shaft so that its large turning resistance keeps the speed steady
the force acting per unit cross sectional area of a stretched or compressed material
items.s: terminal speed: the steady rate of fall reached when the upward drag balances the weight of a falling body. The other options describe stress, Bernoulli theorem, flywheel.

items.q: Which term is described by “the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart”?
o: stress
breaking strength
elastic limit
ductility
items.s: breaking strength is the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart.

items.q: unstable equilibrium may be defined as
o: the product of a force and the time for which it acts
the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track
the point about which a floating body begins to turn when tilted slightly
a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement
items.s: unstable equilibrium: a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement. The other options describe metacentre, impulse, tangential speed.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines period distance relation.
o: the rule that the volume delivered through a narrow tube varies as the fourth power of the radius
the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point
two equal and opposite parallel forces whose lines of action do not coincide
the rule that the square of the time of one circuit varies as the cube of the radius
items.s: period distance relation: the rule that the square of the time of one circuit varies as the cube of the radius. The other options describe Poiseuille law, gravitational potential, couple.

items.q: The statement “the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time” describes which of the following?
o: angular acceleration
uniform circular motion
centripetal force
angular displacement
items.s: angular acceleration is the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time.

items.q: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 0.25 m moves with a speed of 4 m/s. Calculate the angular speed of the wheel in rad/s.
items.s: Angular speed = speed of the rim / radius = 4 / 0.25 = 16 rad/s.

items.q: A force of 30 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.5 m at 45 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 30 x 0.5 x sin 45 degrees = 10.61 N m.

items.q: A solid sphere of mass 4 kg and radius 0.2 m turns about a diameter. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a solid sphere about a diameter the value is two fifths of the mass times the radius squared, giving 0.064.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.5 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 8 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 8 x 0.5 = 4 m/s.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 5 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 1000 N at 1.5 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 1000 x 3.5 / 5 = 700 N.

items.q: A wire of original length 2 m is stretched by 2 mm. Calculate the tensile strain produced.
items.s: Strain is the extension divided by the original length = 0.002 / 2 = 0.001.

items.q: A load of 50 N hangs on a wire of cross sectional area 1.5 x 10^-6 m squared. Calculate the stress in the wire in units of 10^6 Pa.
items.s: Stress = force / area = 50 / (1.5 x 10^-6) = 33.33 units of 10^6 Pa.

items.q: A body of volume 800 cm cubed is fully immersed in water of density 1000 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the upthrust on the body in N.
items.s: The upthrust equals the weight of water displaced = 1000 x (800 x 10^-6) x 9.8 = 7.84 N.

items.q: A tank contains water and has a small hole 1.8 m below the surface. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the speed at which the water leaves the hole in m/s.
items.s: The water leaves with the speed gained in falling that depth, the square root of 2 x 9.8 x 1.8 = 5.94 m/s.

items.q: A body of mass 3 kg moving at 3 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 2 kg and the two move off together. Calculate their common speed in m/s.
items.s: Momentum before equals momentum after, so the common speed is 3 x 3 / (3 + 2) = 1.8 m/s.

items.q: A flywheel turns at a steady angular speed of 52 rad/s for 9 s. Calculate the angle turned through in radians.
items.s: Angle turned = angular speed x time = 52 x 9 = 468 rad.

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 276 rad/s in 3 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 276 / 3 = 92 rad/s squared.

items.q: A body of mass 16 kg moves in a circle of radius 10 m at a steady speed of 17 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it in N.
items.s: Centripetal force = mass x speed squared / radius = 16 x 17 x 17 / 10 = 462.4 N.

items.q: A force of 250 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.6 m from the axis of a nut. Calculate the turning moment about the axis in N m.
items.s: Turning moment = force x perpendicular distance = 250 x 0.6 = 150 N m.

items.q: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. A mass of 40 g hangs 45 cm from the pivot on one side. At what distance in cm from the pivot must a mass of 100 g be hung on the other side to balance the rule?
items.s: Balancing the turning effects, 40 x 45 = 100 x d, so d = 1800/100 = 18 cm.

items.q: Two equal and opposite forces of 10 N each act at two points 0.4 m apart on a body. Calculate the turning effect of the couple in N m.
items.s: The turning effect of a couple is one force times the full separation of the two lines of action, so 10 x 0.8 = 8 N m.

items.q: A uniform disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.8 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its face. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a disc about its central axis the moment of inertia is half the mass times the radius squared, so 2 x 0.8 x 0.8 / 2 = 0.64.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 5 kg and length 2 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a rod about its centre the value is mass times length squared divided by 12 = 5 x 2 x 2 / 12 = 1.67.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 2.5 kg and length 0.8 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 2.5 x 0.8 x 0.8 / 3 = 0.5333.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of mass 1 kg has a moment of inertia of 0.4 kg m squared about an axis through its centre of mass. Calculate its moment of inertia about a parallel axis 0.4 m from that one, in kg m squared.
items.s: The parallel axis rule adds mass times the square of the separation: 0.4 + 1 x 0.4 x 0.4 = 0.56.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 1.2 kg m squared turns at 3 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 1.2 x 3 = 3.6 kg m squared per s.

items.q: A solid disc of mass 2.5 kg rolls without slipping along a level surface at 6 m/s. Calculate its total kinetic energy in J.
items.s: A rolling disc carries half its energy as motion of the centre and half as turning, so the total is three quarters of the mass times the speed squared = 67.5 J.

items.q: A flywheel of moment of inertia 2 kg m squared turns at 8 rad/s. Calculate its rotational kinetic energy in J.
items.s: Rotational kinetic energy = half the moment of inertia times the angular speed squared = 2 x 8 x 8 / 2 = 64 J.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 5 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 500 N at 2 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 500 x 3 / 5 = 300 N.

items.q: Two planets of masses 4 x 10^24 kg and 2 x 10^22 kg have their centres 2 x 10^8 m apart. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the force between them in units of 10^19 N.
items.s: Force = gravitational constant x product of the masses / distance squared = 6.67 x 4 x 2 / (2 x 2) = 13.34 units of 10^19 N.

items.q: A planet has a mass of 3 x 10^22 kg and a radius of 4 x 10^6 m. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the escape speed from its surface in km/s.
items.s: Escape speed is the square root of twice the gravitational constant times the mass divided by the radius, giving 1 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 5 x 10^6 m about a planet of mass 6 x 10^25 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate its orbital speed in km/s.
items.s: Orbital speed is the square root of the gravitational constant times the planet mass divided by the orbit radius, giving 28.29 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 4 x 10^7 m about a planet of mass 2 x 10^25 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared and pi as 3.142, calculate the period of the orbit in hours.
items.s: The period is twice pi times the square root of the cube of the radius divided by the gravitational constant times the planet mass, which is 12.09 hours.

items.q: A planet moves round the sun at a mean distance of 1 x 10^11 m with a period of 4 years. A second planet moves at 9 x 10^11 m. Calculate the period of the second planet in years.
items.s: The square of the period varies as the cube of the radius, so the new period is 4 x (9/1) raised to 1.5 = 108 years.

items.q: A wire of length 2.5 m and cross sectional area 3 x 10^-6 m squared extends by 1.5 mm when a load of 80 N hangs on it. Calculate the Young modulus of the material in units of 10^10 Pa.
items.s: Stress = 80 / (3 x 10^-6) and strain = 1.5 x 10^-3 / 2.5, so the modulus is stress divided by strain = 4.44 units of 10^10 Pa.

items.q: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 12 m below the surface of a liquid of density 13600 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and give your answer in kPa.
items.s: Pressure = density x g x depth = 13600 x 9.8 x 12 = 1599 kPa.

items.q: A pressure of 300 Pa acts on a surface of area 0.05 m squared. Calculate the force acting normally on the surface in N.
items.s: Force = pressure x area = 300 x 0.05 = 15 N.

items.q: Water flows along a pipe of cross sectional area 20 cm squared at 4 m/s. The pipe narrows to a cross sectional area of 8 cm squared. Calculate the speed of the water in the narrow section in m/s.
items.s: The product of area and speed is constant, so the new speed is 20 x 4 / 8 = 10 m/s.

items.q: A liquid of density 800 kg/m cubed is forced through a horizontal pipe by a pressure difference of 3000 Pa. Calculate the speed it attains in m/s.
items.s: The pressure difference appears as kinetic energy per unit volume, so the speed is the square root of 2 x 3000 / 800 = 2.74 m/s.

items.q: A liquid flows through a pipe of cross sectional area 20 cm squared at a speed of 1.5 m/s. Calculate the volume delivered per second in cm cubed per s.
items.s: Volume per second = area x speed = 20 cm squared x 1.5 m/s, with 1.5 m equal to 150 cm, giving 30 cm cubed per s.

items.q: A trolley of mass 2 kg moves at 5 m/s. Calculate its linear momentum in kg m/s.
items.s: Linear momentum = mass x velocity = 2 x 5 = 10 kg m/s.

items.q: A force acts for 0.01 s on a body of mass 1.5 kg and changes its speed from 4 m/s to 15 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the force in N.
items.s: Impulse equals change of momentum, so force = 1.5 x (15 - 4) / 0.01 = 1650 N.

items.q: A ball moving at 6 m/s overtakes another moving at 1 m/s in the same direction. If the coefficient of restitution is 0.75, calculate their relative speed of separation in m/s.
items.s: Relative speed of separation = coefficient of restitution x relative speed of approach = 0.75 x (6 - 1) = 3.75 m/s.

items.q: An engine runs at 120 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed in radians per second, taking pi as 3.142.
items.s: One revolution is 2 x 3.142 rad and one minute is 60 s, so the angular speed is (120 x 6.284)/60 = 12.57 rad/s.

items.q: A force of 75 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.3 m at 30 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 75 x 0.3 x sin 30 degrees = 11.25 N m.

items.q: A solid sphere of mass 3 kg and radius 0.25 m turns about a diameter. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a solid sphere about a diameter the value is two fifths of the mass times the radius squared, giving 0.075.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.3 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 4 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 4 x 0.3 = 1.2 m/s.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 8 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 300 N at 2 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 300 x 6 / 8 = 225 N.

items.q: A wire of original length 1 m is stretched by 0.2 mm. Calculate the tensile strain produced.
items.s: Strain is the extension divided by the original length = 0.0002 / 1 = 0.0002.

items.q: A load of 200 N hangs on a wire of cross sectional area 1.5 x 10^-6 m squared. Calculate the stress in the wire in units of 10^6 Pa.
items.s: Stress = force / area = 200 / (1.5 x 10^-6) = 133.3 units of 10^6 Pa.

items.q: A body of volume 2000 cm cubed is fully immersed in water of density 1000 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the upthrust on the body in N.
items.s: The upthrust equals the weight of water displaced = 1000 x (2000 x 10^-6) x 9.8 = 19.6 N.

items.q: A solid of mass 50 g has a volume of 125 cm cubed. Calculate its density relative to water.
items.s: Relative density is the mass in grams divided by the volume in cm cubed, so 50 / 125 = 0.4.

items.q: A tank contains water and has a small hole 0.8 m below the surface. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the speed at which the water leaves the hole in m/s.
items.s: The water leaves with the speed gained in falling that depth, the square root of 2 x 9.8 x 0.8 = 3.96 m/s.

items.q: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 3 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 2.5 kg and the two move off together. Calculate their common speed in m/s.
items.s: Momentum before equals momentum after, so the common speed is 2 x 3 / (2 + 2.5) = 1.33 m/s.

items.q: A flywheel turns at a steady angular speed of 10 rad/s for 12 s. Calculate the angle turned through in radians.
items.s: Angle turned = angular speed x time = 10 x 12 = 120 rad.

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 96 rad/s in 2 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 96 / 2 = 48 rad/s squared.

items.q: A body of mass 7 kg moves in a circle of radius 10 m at a steady speed of 18 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it in N.
items.s: Centripetal force = mass x speed squared / radius = 7 x 18 x 18 / 10 = 226.8 N.

items.q: A force of 80 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.5 m from the axis of a nut. Calculate the turning moment about the axis in N m.
items.s: Turning moment = force x perpendicular distance = 80 x 0.5 = 40 N m.

items.q: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. A mass of 40 g hangs 25 cm from the pivot on one side. At what distance in cm from the pivot must a mass of 60 g be hung on the other side to balance the rule?
items.s: Balancing the turning effects, 40 x 25 = 60 x d, so d = 1000/60 = 16.67 cm.

items.q: Two equal and opposite forces of 15 N each act at two points 0.2 m apart on a body. Calculate the turning effect of the couple in N m.
items.s: The turning effect of a couple is one force times the full separation of the two lines of action, so 15 x 0.4 = 6 N m.

items.q: A uniform disc of mass 6 kg and radius 0.3 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its face. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a disc about its central axis the moment of inertia is half the mass times the radius squared, so 6 x 0.3 x 0.3 / 2 = 0.27.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 2 kg and length 0.6 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a rod about its centre the value is mass times length squared divided by 12 = 2 x 0.6 x 0.6 / 12 = 0.06.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 4 kg and length 1.2 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 4 x 1.2 x 1.2 / 3 = 1.92.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of mass 4 kg has a moment of inertia of 1.2 kg m squared about an axis through its centre of mass. Calculate its moment of inertia about a parallel axis 0.5 m from that one, in kg m squared.
items.s: The parallel axis rule adds mass times the square of the separation: 1.2 + 4 x 0.5 x 0.5 = 2.2.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 1.5 kg m squared turns at 10 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 1.5 x 10 = 15 kg m squared per s.

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 2 kg and length 1.2 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 2 x 1.2 x 1.2 / 3 = 0.96.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A solid disc of mass 2.5 kg rolls without slipping along a level surface at 8 m/s. Calculate its total kinetic energy in J.
items.s: A rolling disc carries half its energy as motion of the centre and half as turning, so the total is three quarters of the mass times the speed squared = 120 J.

items.q: Two planets of masses 2 x 10^24 kg and 2 x 10^22 kg have their centres 2 x 10^8 m apart. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the force between them in units of 10^19 N.
items.s: Force = gravitational constant x product of the masses / distance squared = 6.67 x 2 x 2 / (2 x 2) = 6.67 units of 10^19 N.

items.q: A planet has a mass of 6 x 10^22 kg and a radius of 4 x 10^6 m. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the escape speed from its surface in km/s.
items.s: Escape speed is the square root of twice the gravitational constant times the mass divided by the radius, giving 1.41 km/s.

items.q: A wire of length 1.5 m and cross sectional area 2.5 x 10^-6 m squared extends by 1 mm when a load of 80 N hangs on it. Calculate the Young modulus of the material in units of 10^10 Pa.
items.s: Stress = 80 / (2.5 x 10^-6) and strain = 1 x 10^-3 / 1.5, so the modulus is stress divided by strain = 4.8 units of 10^10 Pa.

items.q: A liquid of density 1200 kg/m cubed is forced through a horizontal pipe by a pressure difference of 3000 Pa. Calculate the speed it attains in m/s.
items.s: The pressure difference appears as kinetic energy per unit volume, so the speed is the square root of 2 x 3000 / 1200 = 2.24 m/s.

items.q: A force acts for 0.02 s on a body of mass 2 kg and changes its speed from 2 m/s to 15 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the force in N.
items.s: Impulse equals change of momentum, so force = 2 x (15 - 2) / 0.02 = 1300 N.

items.q: A flywheel turns at a steady angular speed of 34 rad/s for 13 s. Calculate the angle turned through in radians.
items.s: Angle turned = angular speed x time = 34 x 13 = 442 rad.

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 132 rad/s in 8 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 132 / 8 = 16.5 rad/s squared.

items.q: An engine runs at 60 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed in radians per second, taking pi as 3.142.
items.s: One revolution is 2 x 3.142 rad and one minute is 60 s, so the angular speed is (60 x 6.284)/60 = 6.28 rad/s.

items.q: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 0.8 m moves with a speed of 2 m/s. Calculate the angular speed of the wheel in rad/s.
items.s: Angular speed = speed of the rim / radius = 2 / 0.8 = 2.5 rad/s.

items.q: A force of 30 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.6 m from the axis of a nut. Calculate the turning moment about the axis in N m.
items.s: Turning moment = force x perpendicular distance = 30 x 0.6 = 18 N m.

items.q: A force of 40 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.25 m at 60 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 40 x 0.25 x sin 60 degrees = 8.66 N m.

items.q: A uniform disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.6 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its face. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a disc about its central axis the moment of inertia is half the mass times the radius squared, so 2 x 0.6 x 0.6 / 2 = 0.36.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of mass 4 kg has a moment of inertia of 1.2 kg m squared about an axis through its centre of mass. Calculate its moment of inertia about a parallel axis 0.4 m from that one, in kg m squared.
items.s: The parallel axis rule adds mass times the square of the separation: 1.2 + 4 x 0.4 x 0.4 = 1.84.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 0.6 kg m squared turns at 4 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 0.6 x 4 = 2.4 kg m squared per s.

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.25 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 6 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 6 x 0.25 = 1.5 m/s.

items.q: A flywheel of moment of inertia 1 kg m squared turns at 15 rad/s. Calculate its rotational kinetic energy in J.
items.s: Rotational kinetic energy = half the moment of inertia times the angular speed squared = 1 x 15 x 15 / 2 = 112.5 J.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 6 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 800 N at 2 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 800 x 4 / 6 = 533.3 N.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 8 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 500 N at 3 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 500 x 5 / 8 = 312.5 N.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 5 x 10^6 m about a planet of mass 3 x 10^23 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate its orbital speed in km/s.
items.s: Orbital speed is the square root of the gravitational constant times the planet mass divided by the orbit radius, giving 2 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 8 x 10^6 m about a planet of mass 6 x 10^25 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared and pi as 3.142, calculate the period of the orbit in hours.
items.s: The period is twice pi times the square root of the cube of the radius divided by the gravitational constant times the planet mass, which is 0.6244 hours.

items.q: A planet moves round the sun at a mean distance of 3 x 10^11 m with a period of 5 years. A second planet moves at 8 x 10^11 m. Calculate the period of the second planet in years.
items.s: The square of the period varies as the cube of the radius, so the new period is 5 x (8/3) raised to 1.5 = 21.77 years.

items.q: A load of 100 N hangs on a wire of cross sectional area 2 x 10^-6 m squared. Calculate the stress in the wire in units of 10^6 Pa.
items.s: Stress = force / area = 100 / (2 x 10^-6) = 50 units of 10^6 Pa.

items.q: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 15 m below the surface of a liquid of density 1000 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and give your answer in kPa.
items.s: Pressure = density x g x depth = 1000 x 9.8 x 15 = 147 kPa.

items.q: A body of volume 200 cm cubed is fully immersed in water of density 1000 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the upthrust on the body in N.
items.s: The upthrust equals the weight of water displaced = 1000 x (200 x 10^-6) x 9.8 = 1.96 N.

items.q: A pressure of 300 Pa acts on a surface of area 0.2 m squared. Calculate the force acting normally on the surface in N.
items.s: Force = pressure x area = 300 x 0.2 = 60 N.

items.q: A solid of mass 50 g has a volume of 200 cm cubed. Calculate its density relative to water.
items.s: Relative density is the mass in grams divided by the volume in cm cubed, so 50 / 200 = 0.25.

items.q: Water flows along a pipe of cross sectional area 40 cm squared at 1.5 m/s. The pipe narrows to a cross sectional area of 4 cm squared. Calculate the speed of the water in the narrow section in m/s.
items.s: The product of area and speed is constant, so the new speed is 40 x 1.5 / 4 = 15 m/s.

items.q: A body of mass 2.5 kg moving at 5 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 2.5 kg and the two move off together. Calculate their common speed in m/s.
items.s: Momentum before equals momentum after, so the common speed is 2.5 x 5 / (2.5 + 2.5) = 2.5 m/s.

items.q: A ball moving at 8 m/s overtakes another moving at 1 m/s in the same direction. If the coefficient of restitution is 0.6, calculate their relative speed of separation in m/s.
items.s: Relative speed of separation = coefficient of restitution x relative speed of approach = 0.6 x (8 - 1) = 4.2 m/s.

items.q: A body of mass 6 kg moves in a circle of radius 6 m at a steady speed of 9 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it in N.
items.s: Centripetal force = mass x speed squared / radius = 6 x 9 x 9 / 6 = 81 N.

items.q: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. A mass of 80 g hangs 30 cm from the pivot on one side. At what distance in cm from the pivot must a mass of 40 g be hung on the other side to balance the rule?
items.s: Balancing the turning effects, 80 x 30 = 40 x d, so d = 2400/40 = 60 cm.

items.q: Two equal and opposite forces of 30 N each act at two points 0.2 m apart on a body. Calculate the turning effect of the couple in N m.
items.s: The turning effect of a couple is one force times the full separation of the two lines of action, so 30 x 0.4 = 12 N m.

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 1 kg and length 0.8 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 1 x 0.8 x 0.8 / 3 = 0.2133.

items.q: A solid disc of mass 2 kg rolls without slipping along a level surface at 2 m/s. Calculate its total kinetic energy in J.

items.q: Two planets of masses 2.5 x 10^24 kg and 1.5 x 10^22 kg have their centres 3 x 10^8 m apart. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the force between them in units of 10^19 N.
items.s: Force = gravitational constant x product of the masses / distance squared = 6.67 x 2.5 x 1.5 / (3 x 3) = 2.78 units of 10^19 N.

items.q: A planet has a mass of 6 x 10^24 kg and a radius of 7 x 10^7 m. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the escape speed from its surface in km/s.
items.s: Escape speed is the square root of twice the gravitational constant times the mass divided by the radius, giving 3.38 km/s.

items.q: A wire of length 2.5 m and cross sectional area 3 x 10^-6 m squared extends by 0.5 mm when a load of 80 N hangs on it. Calculate the Young modulus of the material in units of 10^10 Pa.
items.s: Stress = 80 / (3 x 10^-6) and strain = 0.5 x 10^-3 / 2.5, so the modulus is stress divided by strain = 13.33 units of 10^10 Pa.

items.q: A liquid of density 1000 kg/m cubed is forced through a horizontal pipe by a pressure difference of 2000 Pa. Calculate the speed it attains in m/s.
items.s: The pressure difference appears as kinetic energy per unit volume, so the speed is the square root of 2 x 2000 / 1000 = 2 m/s.

items.q: A force acts for 0.05 s on a body of mass 1 kg and changes its speed from 3 m/s to 10 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the force in N.
items.s: Impulse equals change of momentum, so force = 1 x (10 - 3) / 0.05 = 140 N.

items.q: A flywheel turns at a steady angular speed of 10 rad/s for 14 s. Calculate the angle turned through in radians.
items.s: Angle turned = angular speed x time = 10 x 14 = 140 rad.

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 396 rad/s in 2 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 396 / 2 = 198 rad/s squared.

items.q: An engine runs at 360 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed in radians per second, taking pi as 3.142.
items.s: One revolution is 2 x 3.142 rad and one minute is 60 s, so the angular speed is (360 x 6.284)/60 = 37.7 rad/s.

items.q: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 0.2 m moves with a speed of 10 m/s. Calculate the angular speed of the wheel in rad/s.
items.s: Angular speed = speed of the rim / radius = 10 / 0.2 = 50 rad/s.

items.q: A force of 120 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 1.2 m from the axis of a nut. Calculate the turning moment about the axis in N m.
items.s: Turning moment = force x perpendicular distance = 120 x 1.2 = 144 N m.

items.q: A force of 30 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.5 m at 30 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 30 x 0.5 x sin 30 degrees = 7.5 N m.

items.q: A uniform disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its face. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.

items.q: A solid sphere of mass 1 kg and radius 0.5 m turns about a diameter. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.

items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of mass 3 kg has a moment of inertia of 2 kg m squared about an axis through its centre of mass. Calculate its moment of inertia about a parallel axis 0.2 m from that one, in kg m squared.
