items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 0.6 kg m squared turns at 5 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 0.6 x 5 = 3 kg m squared per s.

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.6 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 15 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 15 x 0.6 = 9 m/s.

items.q: A flywheel of moment of inertia 0.5 kg m squared turns at 4 rad/s. Calculate its rotational kinetic energy in J.
items.s: Rotational kinetic energy = half the moment of inertia times the angular speed squared = 0.5 x 4 x 4 / 2 = 4 J.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 6 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 500 N at 1.5 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 500 x 4.5 / 6 = 375 N.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 5 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 200 N at 2 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 200 x 3 / 5 = 120 N.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 7 x 10^6 m about a planet of mass 3 x 10^25 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate its orbital speed in km/s.
items.s: Orbital speed is the square root of the gravitational constant times the planet mass divided by the orbit radius, giving 16.91 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 8 x 10^7 m about a planet of mass 3 x 10^23 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared and pi as 3.142, calculate the period of the orbit in hours.
items.s: The period is twice pi times the square root of the cube of the radius divided by the gravitational constant times the planet mass, which is 279.2 hours.

items.q: A planet moves round the sun at a mean distance of 1 x 10^11 m with a period of 5 years. A second planet moves at 12 x 10^11 m. Calculate the period of the second planet in years.
items.s: The square of the period varies as the cube of the radius, so the new period is 5 x (12/1) raised to 1.5 = 207.8 years.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines buoyancy law.
o: the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
the upward push of a fluid on a body partly or wholly immersed in it
the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water
the rule that the upward push equals the weight of fluid displaced by an immersed body
items.s: buoyancy law: the rule that the upward push equals the weight of fluid displaced by an immersed body. The other options describe upthrust, atmospheric pressure, relative density.

items.q: unstable equilibrium is best described as
o: the overturning of a body when a vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base
a resting state in which a body displaced slightly stays at rest in its new position
a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement
the point through which the total weight of a body may be taken to act
items.s: unstable equilibrium: a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement. The other options describe centre of gravity, toppling, neutral equilibrium.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the turning of a body about an axis that passes through its own centre”
o: condition for pure rolling
gyroscope
spin
rolling motion
items.s: spin is the turning of a body about an axis that passes through its own centre.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel”
o: angular displacement
uniform circular motion
period of revolution
centripetal force
items.s: uniform circular motion is movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the angle through which a turning body swings, measured in radians about its axis”
o: uniform circular motion
angular acceleration
period of revolution
angular displacement
items.s: angular displacement is the angle through which a turning body swings, measured in radians about its axis.

items.q: mass element may be defined as
o: a very small portion of a body treated as a point when summing contributions about an axis
the rule that two values taken in the plane of a thin flat sheet add to the value about its normal
the distance from the axis at which the whole mass could be placed to give the same turning resistance
the way the material of a body is spread out relative to the axis about which it turns
items.s: mass element: a very small portion of a body treated as a point when summing contributions about an axis. The other options describe mass distribution, perpendicular axis theorem, radius of gyration.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: Which of the following best describes tangential speed?
o: the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
the angle through which a turning body swings, measured in radians about its axis
the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track
the inward pull on a body moving in a circle that keeps it on its curved path
items.s: tangential speed: the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track. The other options describe angular displacement, angular velocity, centripetal force.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Circular motion and angular kinematics?
o: angular velocity
stress
angular displacement
angular acceleration
items.s: Every other option belongs to Circular motion and angular kinematics. “stress” belongs to Elasticity of solids, not Circular motion and angular kinematics.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines precession?
o: the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone
one complete journey of a body round an external centre
a rapidly spinning heavy wheel whose axis keeps its direction when the frame is tilted
the turning of a body about an axis that passes through its own centre
items.s: precession: the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone. The other options describe gyroscope, revolution, spin.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the overturning of a body when a vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base”
o: toppling
unstable equilibrium
stable equilibrium
metacentre
items.s: toppling is the overturning of a body when a vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base.

items.q: density is best described as
o: a U shaped tube of liquid used to compare the pressure of a gas with that of the air
the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water
the quantity of matter contained in unit volume of a substance
the force acting normally per unit area on a surface
items.s: density: the quantity of matter contained in unit volume of a substance. The other options describe manometer, relative density, pressure.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Angular momentum and rolling motion?
o: rolling motion
equation of continuity
angular momentum
conservation of angular momentum
items.s: Every other option belongs to Angular momentum and rolling motion. “equation of continuity” belongs to Fluid dynamics, not Angular momentum and rolling motion.

items.q: Which of the following best describes linear momentum?
o: a very large push acting for a very short time, changing momentum appreciably
the product of the mass of a body and its velocity
the principle that the total quantity of motion of an isolated system does not change during an interaction
the ratio of the relative rate of separation after a bounce to the relative rate of approach before it
items.s: linear momentum: the product of the mass of a body and its velocity. The other options describe conservation of linear momentum, coefficient of restitution, impulsive force.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines angular acceleration.
o: the angle through which a turning body swings, measured in radians about its axis
the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
the inward pull on a body moving in a circle that keeps it on its curved path
the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time
items.s: angular acceleration: the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time. The other options describe angular velocity, centripetal force, angular displacement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines precession.
o: the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone
the requirement that the speed of the centre equals the product of the angular rate and the radius
one complete journey of a body round an external centre
the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts
items.s: precession: the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone. The other options describe condition for pure rolling, revolution, conservation of angular momentum.

items.q: rolling motion is best described as
o: the product of the turning resistance of a body about an axis and its rate of turning about that axis
the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts
movement of a round body along a surface while it also turns about its own axis
a rapidly spinning heavy wheel whose axis keeps its direction when the frame is tilted
items.s: rolling motion: movement of a round body along a surface while it also turns about its own axis. The other options describe gyroscope, conservation of angular momentum, angular momentum.

items.q: Which of the following best describes principle of moments?
o: two equal and opposite parallel forces whose lines of action do not coincide
the fixed line about which every point of a turning body moves in a circle
the rate at which a turning effect does work on a rotating body
the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
items.s: principle of moments: the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect. The other options describe couple, axis of rotation, rotational power.

items.q: Which term is described by “the inward pull on a body moving in a circle that keeps it on its curved path”?
o: period of revolution
tangential speed
centripetal force
uniform circular motion
items.s: centripetal force is the inward pull on a body moving in a circle that keeps it on its curved path.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a resting state in which a small displacement creates a restoring turning effect back to the original position”
o: neutral equilibrium
metacentre
toppling
stable equilibrium
items.s: stable equilibrium is a resting state in which a small displacement creates a restoring turning effect back to the original position.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Fluid dynamics?
o: streamline
viscosity
yield point
turbulent flow
items.s: Every other option belongs to Fluid dynamics. “yield point” belongs to Elasticity of solids, not Fluid dynamics.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water”?
o: upthrust
manometer
relative density
buoyancy law
items.s: relative density is the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water.

items.q: conservation of linear momentum is best described as
o: the product of the mass of a body and its velocity
the principle that the total quantity of motion of an isolated system does not change during an interaction
the product of a force and the time for which it acts
a head-on meeting of bodies after which they move together with some kinetic energy lost as heat
items.s: conservation of linear momentum: the principle that the total quantity of motion of an isolated system does not change during an interaction. The other options describe linear momentum, impulse, inelastic collision.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Gravitation and satellite motion?
o: moment arm
escape speed
gravitational field strength
universal gravitational attraction
items.s: Every other option belongs to Gravitation and satellite motion. “moment arm” belongs to Torque and rotational dynamics, not Gravitation and satellite motion.

items.q: torque is best described as
o: the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
the fixed line about which every point of a turning body moves in a circle
two equal and opposite parallel forces whose lines of action do not coincide
the turning effect of a force about an axis, equal to the force times its perpendicular distance from that axis
items.s: torque: the turning effect of a force about an axis, equal to the force times its perpendicular distance from that axis. The other options describe axis of rotation, principle of moments, couple.

items.q: yield point is best described as
o: the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart
the ratio of the force per unit area to the fractional extension of a wire, a measure of stiffness
the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull
the force acting per unit cross sectional area of a stretched or compressed material
items.s: yield point: the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull. The other options describe Young modulus, stress, breaking strength.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines gravitational field strength.
o: the pull per unit mass experienced by a small body placed at a point
the rule that the pull between two masses falls as the square of the distance between their centres
the least launch rate needed for a body to leave a planet and never come back
the rate at which a satellite travels along its closed path about a central body
items.s: gravitational field strength: the pull per unit mass experienced by a small body placed at a point. The other options describe escape speed, orbital speed, universal gravitational attraction.

items.q: Which term is described by “the state in which the total turning effect on a body about any axis is zero”?
o: principle of moments
torque
rotational equilibrium
axis of rotation
items.s: rotational equilibrium is the state in which the total turning effect on a body about any axis is zero.

items.q: Which of the following best describes radius of gyration?
o: the sum of the products of each mass element of a body and the square of its distance from the axis
a flat sheet whose depth is negligible compared with its length and breadth
the distance from the axis at which the whole mass could be placed to give the same turning resistance
the way the material of a body is spread out relative to the axis about which it turns
items.s: radius of gyration: the distance from the axis at which the whole mass could be placed to give the same turning resistance. The other options describe moment of inertia, thin lamina, mass distribution.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines uniform circular motion.
o: movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel
the angle through which a turning body swings, measured in radians about its axis
the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track
items.s: uniform circular motion: movement of a body round a closed curve at a constant rate of travel. The other options describe angular displacement, tangential speed, angular velocity.

items.q: inelastic collision is best described as
o: the ratio of the relative rate of separation after a bounce to the relative rate of approach before it
the product of the mass of a body and its velocity
a head-on meeting of bodies after which they move together with some kinetic energy lost as heat
a very large push acting for a very short time, changing momentum appreciably
items.s: inelastic collision: a head-on meeting of bodies after which they move together with some kinetic energy lost as heat. The other options describe linear momentum, coefficient of restitution, impulsive force.

items.q: pressure is best described as
o: the rule that the upward push equals the weight of fluid displaced by an immersed body
the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
the force acting normally per unit area on a surface
the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water
items.s: pressure: the force acting normally per unit area on a surface. The other options describe buoyancy law, atmospheric pressure, relative density.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines brittleness.
o: the ratio of the force per unit area to the fractional extension of a wire, a measure of stiffness
the tendency of a material to snap with little stretching once its limit is passed
the greatest load a material can bear and still return to its original shape when unloaded
the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull
items.s: brittleness: the tendency of a material to snap with little stretching once its limit is passed. The other options describe yield point, elastic limit, Young modulus.

items.q: Which term is described by “one complete journey of a body round an external centre”?
o: gyroscope
rolling motion
revolution
conservation of angular momentum
items.s: revolution is one complete journey of a body round an external centre.

items.q: Which term is described by “the overturning of a body when a vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base”?
o: centre of gravity
toppling
stable equilibrium
neutral equilibrium
items.s: toppling is the overturning of a body when a vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base.

items.q: Which of the following best describes unstable equilibrium?
o: the overturning of a body when a vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base
the point about which a floating body begins to turn when tilted slightly
a resting state in which a body displaced slightly stays at rest in its new position
a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement
items.s: unstable equilibrium: a resting state in which a small displacement creates a turning effect that increases the displacement. The other options describe metacentre, neutral equilibrium, toppling.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines rotational power.
o: the state in which the total turning effect on a body about any axis is zero
the rate at which a turning effect does work on a rotating body
the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
the turning effect of a force about an axis, equal to the force times its perpendicular distance from that axis
items.s: rotational power: the rate at which a turning effect does work on a rotating body. The other options describe principle of moments, rotational equilibrium, torque.

items.q: Which of the following best describes period of revolution?
o: the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track
the time taken by a body moving on a closed path to complete one full circuit
the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time
the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
items.s: period of revolution: the time taken by a body moving on a closed path to complete one full circuit. The other options describe radian, tangential speed, angular acceleration.

items.q: Which of the following best describes angular velocity?
o: the time taken by a body moving on a closed path to complete one full circuit
the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
the inward pull on a body moving in a circle that keeps it on its curved path
the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
items.s: angular velocity: the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time. The other options describe centripetal force, radian, period of revolution.

items.q: Which of the following best describes gravitational potential?
o: the rule that the square of the time of one circuit varies as the cube of the radius
the least launch rate needed for a body to leave a planet and never come back
the pull per unit mass experienced by a small body placed at a point
the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point
items.s: gravitational potential: the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point. The other options describe escape speed, period distance relation, gravitational field strength.

items.q: moment of inertia is best described as
o: a heavy wheel fixed to a shaft so that its large turning resistance keeps the speed steady
the rule that two values taken in the plane of a thin flat sheet add to the value about its normal
the sum of the products of each mass element of a body and the square of its distance from the axis
the distance from the axis at which the whole mass could be placed to give the same turning resistance
items.s: moment of inertia: the sum of the products of each mass element of a body and the square of its distance from the axis. The other options describe flywheel, perpendicular axis theorem, radius of gyration.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: Which of the following best describes condition for pure rolling?
o: the requirement that the speed of the centre equals the product of the angular rate and the radius
the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts
the turning of a body about an axis that passes through its own centre
the product of the turning resistance of a body about an axis and its rate of turning about that axis
items.s: condition for pure rolling: the requirement that the speed of the centre equals the product of the angular rate and the radius. The other options describe angular momentum, conservation of angular momentum, spin.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the continuous path followed by a small element of a moving fluid”
o: equation of continuity
streamline
Bernoulli theorem
viscosity
items.s: streamline is the continuous path followed by a small element of a moving fluid.

items.q: Which of the following best describes yield point?
o: the force acting per unit cross sectional area of a stretched or compressed material
the ability of a material to be drawn out into a long thin thread
the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull
the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart
items.s: yield point: the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull. The other options describe ductility, breaking strength, stress.

items.q: Which of the following best describes radian?
o: the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time
the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
the angle through which a turning body swings, measured in radians about its axis
items.s: radian: the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius. The other options describe angular displacement, angular velocity, angular acceleration.

items.q: precession is best described as
o: the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts
the product of the turning resistance of a body about an axis and its rate of turning about that axis
movement of a round body along a surface while it also turns about its own axis
the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone
items.s: precession: the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone. The other options describe angular momentum, rolling motion, conservation of angular momentum.

items.q: Which of the following best describes reaction at a support?
o: a resting state in which a small displacement creates a restoring turning effect back to the original position
the point through which the total weight of a body may be taken to act
the upward push that a pillar or wall exerts on a beam resting on it
the point about which a floating body begins to turn when tilted slightly
items.s: reaction at a support: the upward push that a pillar or wall exerts on a beam resting on it. The other options describe stable equilibrium, centre of gravity, metacentre.

items.q: Which of the following best describes stress?
o: the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull
the ratio of the force per unit area to the fractional extension of a wire, a measure of stiffness
the greatest force per unit area a material can carry before it tears apart
the force acting per unit cross sectional area of a stretched or compressed material
items.s: stress: the force acting per unit cross sectional area of a stretched or compressed material. The other options describe breaking strength, Young modulus, yield point.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines radian.
o: the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
the angle through which a turning body swings, measured in radians about its axis
the inward pull on a body moving in a circle that keeps it on its curved path
the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
items.s: radian: the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius. The other options describe angular displacement, centripetal force, angular velocity.

items.q: Which term is described by “the force acting normally per unit area on a surface”?
o: manometer
relative density
hydraulic press
pressure
items.s: pressure is the force acting normally per unit area on a surface.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines gravitational potential.
o: the least launch rate needed for a body to leave a planet and never come back
the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point
the rule that the square of the time of one circuit varies as the cube of the radius
the pull of a planet on a body, equal to the product of its mass and the local field strength
items.s: gravitational potential: the work done per unit mass in bringing a small body from infinity to a point. The other options describe period distance relation, weight, escape speed.

items.q: density may be defined as
o: the rule that the upward push equals the weight of fluid displaced by an immersed body
the quantity of matter contained in unit volume of a substance
the force acting normally per unit area on a surface
the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
items.s: density: the quantity of matter contained in unit volume of a substance. The other options describe buoyancy law, atmospheric pressure, pressure.

items.q: Which term is described by “a rapidly spinning heavy wheel whose axis keeps its direction when the frame is tilted”?
o: gyroscope
conservation of angular momentum
revolution
spin
items.s: gyroscope is a rapidly spinning heavy wheel whose axis keeps its direction when the frame is tilted.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Elasticity of solids?
o: uniform circular motion
Young modulus
stress
strain
items.s: Every other option belongs to Elasticity of solids. “uniform circular motion” belongs to Circular motion and angular kinematics, not Elasticity of solids.

items.q: Three of these relate to Fluid dynamics. Which one does not?
o: streamline
turbulent flow
uniform circular motion
viscosity
items.s: Every other option belongs to Fluid dynamics. “uniform circular motion” belongs to Circular motion and angular kinematics, not Fluid dynamics.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the rule that the product of cross section and speed stays the same along a pipe carrying an incompressible fluid”
o: equation of continuity
Bernoulli theorem
streamline
ideal fluid
items.s: equation of continuity is the rule that the product of cross section and speed stays the same along a pipe carrying an incompressible fluid.

items.q: Which term is described by “the way the material of a body is spread out relative to the axis about which it turns”?
o: parallel axis theorem
mass distribution
mass element
flywheel
items.s: mass distribution is the way the material of a body is spread out relative to the axis about which it turns.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: Which statement correctly defines tangential speed?
o: the rate at which the angle turned by a rotating body changes with time
the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time
the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc equal in length to its radius
the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track
items.s: tangential speed: the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track. The other options describe angular acceleration, angular velocity, radian.

items.q: relative density may be defined as
o: the upward push of a fluid on a body partly or wholly immersed in it
the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
a U shaped tube of liquid used to compare the pressure of a gas with that of the air
the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water
items.s: relative density: the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water. The other options describe atmospheric pressure, upthrust, manometer.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines conservation of angular momentum?
o: the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts
one complete journey of a body round an external centre
the slow sweep of the axis of a spinning body around a cone
the requirement that the speed of the centre equals the product of the angular rate and the radius
items.s: conservation of angular momentum: the principle that the total turning quantity of a system stays constant when no external turning effect acts. The other options describe precession, condition for pure rolling, revolution.

items.q: Which term is described by “the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull”?
o: yield point
ductility
breaking strength
Young modulus
items.s: yield point is the load at which a stretched material suddenly extends without any further increase of pull.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines principle of moments.
o: the fixed line about which every point of a turning body moves in a circle
the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect
the perpendicular distance from the axis of turning to the line along which a force acts
two equal and opposite parallel forces whose lines of action do not coincide
items.s: principle of moments: the rule that a body balances when the total clockwise turning effect equals the total anticlockwise turning effect. The other options describe moment arm, axis of rotation, couple.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines relative density.
o: the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air above a surface
the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water
the upward push of a fluid on a body partly or wholly immersed in it
the quantity of matter contained in unit volume of a substance
items.s: relative density: the ratio of the mass of a substance to the mass of an equal volume of water. The other options describe atmospheric pressure, density, upthrust.

items.q: tangential speed is best described as
o: the rate at which the rate of turning of a body changes with time
the time taken by a body moving on a closed path to complete one full circuit
the inward pull on a body moving in a circle that keeps it on its curved path
the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track
items.s: tangential speed: the rate at which a point on a turning body moves along the edge of its circular track. The other options describe angular acceleration, centripetal force, period of revolution.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines conservation of linear momentum.
o: a very large push acting for a very short time, changing momentum appreciably
a head-on meeting of bodies after which they move together with some kinetic energy lost as heat
the principle that the total quantity of motion of an isolated system does not change during an interaction
a head-on meeting of bodies in which both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
items.s: conservation of linear momentum: the principle that the total quantity of motion of an isolated system does not change during an interaction. The other options describe inelastic collision, elastic collision, impulsive force.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines parallel axis theorem?
o: a very small portion of a body treated as a point when summing contributions about an axis
a flat sheet whose depth is negligible compared with its length and breadth
the rule adding mass times the square of the separation to the value taken through the centre of mass
the rule that two values taken in the plane of a thin flat sheet add to the value about its normal
items.s: parallel axis theorem: the rule adding mass times the square of the separation to the value taken through the centre of mass. The other options describe mass element, thin lamina, perpendicular axis theorem.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A flywheel of moment of inertia 3 kg m squared turns at 4 rad/s. Calculate its rotational kinetic energy in J.
items.s: Rotational kinetic energy = half the moment of inertia times the angular speed squared = 3 x 4 x 4 / 2 = 24 J.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 6 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 200 N at 1.5 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 200 x 4.5 / 6 = 150 N.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 7 x 10^7 m about a planet of mass 4 x 10^24 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate its orbital speed in km/s.
items.s: Orbital speed is the square root of the gravitational constant times the planet mass divided by the orbit radius, giving 1.95 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 6 x 10^6 m about a planet of mass 5 x 10^24 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared and pi as 3.142, calculate the period of the orbit in hours.
items.s: The period is twice pi times the square root of the cube of the radius divided by the gravitational constant times the planet mass, which is 1.4 hours.

items.q: A planet moves round the sun at a mean distance of 1.5 x 10^11 m with a period of 2 years. A second planet moves at 16 x 10^11 m. Calculate the period of the second planet in years.
items.s: The square of the period varies as the cube of the radius, so the new period is 2 x (16/1.5) raised to 1.5 = 69.67 years.

items.q: A ball moving at 5 m/s overtakes another moving at 3 m/s in the same direction. If the coefficient of restitution is 0.75, calculate their relative speed of separation in m/s.
items.s: Relative speed of separation = coefficient of restitution x relative speed of approach = 0.75 x (5 - 3) = 1.5 m/s.

items.q: A flywheel turns at a steady angular speed of 20 rad/s for 9 s. Calculate the angle turned through in radians.
items.s: Angle turned = angular speed x time = 20 x 9 = 180 rad.

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 432 rad/s in 5 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 432 / 5 = 86.4 rad/s squared.

items.q: An engine runs at 420 revolutions per minute. Calculate its angular speed in radians per second, taking pi as 3.142.
items.s: One revolution is 2 x 3.142 rad and one minute is 60 s, so the angular speed is (420 x 6.284)/60 = 43.99 rad/s.

items.q: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 0.8 m moves with a speed of 12 m/s. Calculate the angular speed of the wheel in rad/s.
items.s: Angular speed = speed of the rim / radius = 12 / 0.8 = 15 rad/s.

items.q: A body of mass 3 kg moves in a circle of radius 5 m at a steady speed of 11 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it in N.
items.s: Centripetal force = mass x speed squared / radius = 3 x 11 x 11 / 5 = 72.6 N.

items.q: A force of 120 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.3 m at 60 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 120 x 0.3 x sin 60 degrees = 31.18 N m.

items.q: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. A mass of 60 g hangs 20 cm from the pivot on one side. At what distance in cm from the pivot must a mass of 80 g be hung on the other side to balance the rule?
items.s: Balancing the turning effects, 60 x 20 = 80 x d, so d = 1200/80 = 15 cm.

items.q: Two equal and opposite forces of 50 N each act at two points 0.8 m apart on a body. Calculate the turning effect of the couple in N m.
items.s: The turning effect of a couple is one force times the full separation of the two lines of action, so 50 x 1.6 = 80 N m.

items.q: A solid sphere of mass 3 kg and radius 0.4 m turns about a diameter. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a solid sphere about a diameter the value is two fifths of the mass times the radius squared, giving 0.192.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 2 kg and length 2 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a rod about its centre the value is mass times length squared divided by 12 = 2 x 2 x 2 / 12 = 0.6667.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 1.5 kg and length 0.5 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 1.5 x 0.5 x 0.5 / 3 = 0.125.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 2.5 kg m squared turns at 5 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 2.5 x 5 = 12.5 kg m squared per s.

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.45 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 4 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 4 x 0.45 = 1.8 m/s.

items.q: A solid disc of mass 2 kg rolls without slipping along a level surface at 5 m/s. Calculate its total kinetic energy in J.
items.s: A rolling disc carries half its energy as motion of the centre and half as turning, so the total is three quarters of the mass times the speed squared = 37.5 J.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 4 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 800 N at 3 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 800 x 1 / 4 = 200 N.

items.q: Two planets of masses 2.5 x 10^24 kg and 1 x 10^22 kg have their centres 1.5 x 10^8 m apart. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the force between them in units of 10^19 N.
items.s: Force = gravitational constant x product of the masses / distance squared = 6.67 x 2.5 x 1 / (1.5 x 1.5) = 7.41 units of 10^19 N.

items.q: A planet has a mass of 4 x 10^24 kg and a radius of 5 x 10^5 m. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the escape speed from its surface in km/s.
items.s: Escape speed is the square root of twice the gravitational constant times the mass divided by the radius, giving 32.67 km/s.

items.q: A wire of length 3 m and cross sectional area 1.5 x 10^-6 m squared extends by 0.5 mm when a load of 80 N hangs on it. Calculate the Young modulus of the material in units of 10^10 Pa.
items.s: Stress = 80 / (1.5 x 10^-6) and strain = 0.5 x 10^-3 / 3, so the modulus is stress divided by strain = 32 units of 10^10 Pa.

items.q: A wire of original length 1.5 m is stretched by 0.8 mm. Calculate the tensile strain produced.
items.s: Strain is the extension divided by the original length = 0.0008 / 1.5 = 0.000533.

items.q: A load of 120 N hangs on a wire of cross sectional area 0.5 x 10^-6 m squared. Calculate the stress in the wire in units of 10^6 Pa.
items.s: Stress = force / area = 120 / (0.5 x 10^-6) = 240 units of 10^6 Pa.

items.q: Calculate the pressure at a depth of 10 m below the surface of a liquid of density 1000 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and give your answer in kPa.
items.s: Pressure = density x g x depth = 1000 x 9.8 x 10 = 98 kPa.

items.q: A body of volume 1500 cm cubed is fully immersed in water of density 1000 kg/m cubed. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the upthrust on the body in N.
items.s: The upthrust equals the weight of water displaced = 1000 x (1500 x 10^-6) x 9.8 = 14.7 N.

items.q: A pressure of 200 Pa acts on a surface of area 0.1 m squared. Calculate the force acting normally on the surface in N.
items.s: Force = pressure x area = 200 x 0.1 = 20 N.

items.q: A solid of mass 100 g has a volume of 150 cm cubed. Calculate its density relative to water.
items.s: Relative density is the mass in grams divided by the volume in cm cubed, so 100 / 150 = 0.6667.

items.q: Water flows along a pipe of cross sectional area 20 cm squared at 1.5 m/s. The pipe narrows to a cross sectional area of 2 cm squared. Calculate the speed of the water in the narrow section in m/s.
items.s: The product of area and speed is constant, so the new speed is 20 x 1.5 / 2 = 15 m/s.

items.q: A tank contains water and has a small hole 1.5 m below the surface. Take g as 9.8 m/s squared and calculate the speed at which the water leaves the hole in m/s.
items.s: The water leaves with the speed gained in falling that depth, the square root of 2 x 9.8 x 1.5 = 5.42 m/s.

items.q: A liquid of density 800 kg/m cubed is forced through a horizontal pipe by a pressure difference of 4000 Pa. Calculate the speed it attains in m/s.
items.s: The pressure difference appears as kinetic energy per unit volume, so the speed is the square root of 2 x 4000 / 800 = 3.16 m/s.

items.q: A liquid flows through a pipe of cross sectional area 10 cm squared at a speed of 2.5 m/s. Calculate the volume delivered per second in cm cubed per s.
items.s: Volume per second = area x speed = 10 cm squared x 2.5 m/s, with 2.5 m equal to 250 cm, giving 25 cm cubed per s.

items.q: A trolley of mass 2.5 kg moves at 6 m/s. Calculate its linear momentum in kg m/s.
items.s: Linear momentum = mass x velocity = 2.5 x 6 = 15 kg m/s.

items.q: A body of mass 1.5 kg moving at 2 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 2.5 kg and the two move off together. Calculate their common speed in m/s.
items.s: Momentum before equals momentum after, so the common speed is 1.5 x 2 / (1.5 + 2.5) = 0.75 m/s.

items.q: A force acts for 0.05 s on a body of mass 1 kg and changes its speed from 6 m/s to 30 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the force in N.
items.s: Impulse equals change of momentum, so force = 1 x (30 - 6) / 0.05 = 480 N.

items.q: A body of mass 2 kg has a moment of inertia of 0.5 kg m squared about an axis through its centre of mass. Calculate its moment of inertia about a parallel axis 0.5 m from that one, in kg m squared.
items.s: The parallel axis rule adds mass times the square of the separation: 0.5 + 2 x 0.5 x 0.5 = 1.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A flywheel of moment of inertia 0.5 kg m squared turns at 8 rad/s. Calculate its rotational kinetic energy in J.
items.s: Rotational kinetic energy = half the moment of inertia times the angular speed squared = 0.5 x 8 x 8 / 2 = 16 J.

items.q: A uniform beam of length 4 m rests on two supports at its ends and carries a load of 800 N at 2 m from the left support. Calculate the reaction at the left support in N.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support, the left reaction is load x distance from the right / span = 800 x 2 / 4 = 400 N.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 8 x 10^7 m about a planet of mass 6 x 10^24 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate its orbital speed in km/s.
items.s: Orbital speed is the square root of the gravitational constant times the planet mass divided by the orbit radius, giving 2.24 km/s.

items.q: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 8 x 10^7 m about a planet of mass 8 x 10^24 kg. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared and pi as 3.142, calculate the period of the orbit in hours.
items.s: The period is twice pi times the square root of the cube of the radius divided by the gravitational constant times the planet mass, which is 54.07 hours.

items.q: A planet moves round the sun at a mean distance of 2 x 10^11 m with a period of 5 years. A second planet moves at 16 x 10^11 m. Calculate the period of the second planet in years.
items.s: The square of the period varies as the cube of the radius, so the new period is 5 x (16/2) raised to 1.5 = 113.1 years.

items.q: A ball moving at 4 m/s overtakes another moving at 2 m/s in the same direction. If the coefficient of restitution is 0.6, calculate their relative speed of separation in m/s.
items.s: Relative speed of separation = coefficient of restitution x relative speed of approach = 0.6 x (4 - 2) = 1.2 m/s.

items.q: A flywheel turns at a steady angular speed of 50 rad/s for 7 s. Calculate the angle turned through in radians.
items.s: Angle turned = angular speed x time = 50 x 7 = 350 rad.

items.q: A wheel starting from rest attains an angular speed of 348 rad/s in 4 s. Calculate its angular acceleration in rad/s squared.
items.s: Angular acceleration = change in angular speed / time = 348 / 4 = 87 rad/s squared.

items.q: A point on the rim of a wheel of radius 0.25 m moves with a speed of 5 m/s. Calculate the angular speed of the wheel in rad/s.
items.s: Angular speed = speed of the rim / radius = 5 / 0.25 = 20 rad/s.

items.q: A body of mass 19 kg moves in a circle of radius 9 m at a steady speed of 5 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force on it in N.
items.s: Centripetal force = mass x speed squared / radius = 19 x 5 x 5 / 9 = 52.78 N.

items.q: A force of 25 N is applied to a spanner of length 0.8 m at 30 degrees to the handle. Calculate the turning effect about the nut in N m.
items.s: Turning effect = force x length x sin(angle) = 25 x 0.8 x sin 30 degrees = 10 N m.

items.q: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. A mass of 50 g hangs 45 cm from the pivot on one side. At what distance in cm from the pivot must a mass of 100 g be hung on the other side to balance the rule?
items.s: Balancing the turning effects, 50 x 45 = 100 x d, so d = 2250/100 = 22.5 cm.

items.q: Two equal and opposite forces of 20 N each act at two points 0.6 m apart on a body. Calculate the turning effect of the couple in N m.
items.s: The turning effect of a couple is one force times the full separation of the two lines of action, so 20 x 1.2 = 24 N m.

items.q: A uniform disc of mass 5 kg and radius 0.4 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its face. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a disc about its central axis the moment of inertia is half the mass times the radius squared, so 5 x 0.4 x 0.4 / 2 = 0.4.

items.q: A solid sphere of mass 4 kg and radius 0.3 m turns about a diameter. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a solid sphere about a diameter the value is two fifths of the mass times the radius squared, giving 0.144.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 1 m turns about an axis through its centre perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: For a rod about its centre the value is mass times length squared divided by 12 = 3 x 1 x 1 / 12 = 0.25.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A thin uniform rod of mass 1 kg and length 0.6 m turns about an axis through one end perpendicular to its length. Calculate its moment of inertia in kg m squared.
items.s: About an end the value is mass times length squared divided by 3 = 1 x 0.6 x 0.6 / 3 = 0.12.
items.t: Moment of inertia and its theorems

items.q: A body of moment of inertia 1 kg m squared turns at 8 rad/s about a fixed axis. Calculate its angular momentum in kg m squared per s.
items.s: Angular momentum = moment of inertia x angular speed = 1 x 8 = 8 kg m squared per s.

items.q: A wheel of radius 0.35 m rolls without slipping along a level road with an angular speed of 12 rad/s. Calculate the speed of its centre in m/s.
items.s: For rolling without slipping the speed of the centre is angular speed times radius = 12 x 0.35 = 4.2 m/s.

items.q: A solid disc of mass 1 kg rolls without slipping along a level surface at 2 m/s. Calculate its total kinetic energy in J.
items.s: A rolling disc carries half its energy as motion of the centre and half as turning, so the total is three quarters of the mass times the speed squared = 3 J.

items.q: Two planets of masses 4 x 10^24 kg and 1.5 x 10^22 kg have their centres 3 x 10^8 m apart. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the force between them in units of 10^19 N.
items.s: Force = gravitational constant x product of the masses / distance squared = 6.67 x 4 x 1.5 / (3 x 3) = 4.45 units of 10^19 N.

items.q: A planet has a mass of 3 x 10^22 kg and a radius of 4 x 10^7 m. Taking the gravitational constant as 6.67 x 10^-11 N m squared per kg squared, calculate the escape speed from its surface in km/s.
items.s: Escape speed is the square root of twice the gravitational constant times the mass divided by the radius, giving 0.3163 km/s.
